reason: r25 answers the area-change failure that r24's run showed. r24 (NRO 6a16c5429a15e761db5b4168586343dfa4ca59e19fdb74143fc00cfd1b74994b, Eden 2026-10-24, installed bytes matching) is the first run where the mod's mask did not hide the gauge: the probe read anchors=0xff0, mat starting 0x3f800000 (the transform x scale r24 writes), authored height 128 and a rectangle of 110,38,110,166 with its bottom on the bar's bottom, and the user reported the gauge shown from the quest start. It then disappeared on an area change: at t=149.89 the walker's link check dropped the addresses, the plugin stopped writing, and the mask kept applying its last rectangle, so the new area's gauge was clipped away. r25 disables the scissor on that path, from the mask's own enter handler where the game has handed over a live object, by calling main+0xa4ba20, the class's DTI Enable setter, decoded from the NSO bytes as ldr r2,[r0,#0xa4]; bfc r2,#0,#1; bfc; str; bx lr (it clears the enable bits and ignores the second argument). The draw walker's check stays read-only, per the workspace rule that a write to a game object needs a native lookup in the same callback. The geometry r24 established stays: the rectangle is the game's to build (main+0xa4ba94 rebuilds +0xb0..+0xbc from the quad when bit 1 of +0xa4 is set), the quad comes from main+0xa4b390 with the anchor modes at +0xa0 bits 0-3 and the authored pair multiplied by the transform rows at +0x10/+0x20, and the row's layout zeroes the authored width every frame, so the enter-call write is the width the scissor receives. The insertion has completed five times (r18, r20, r22, r23, r24) with the 5-word object array through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator, the draw block resized through the root's vtable slot 0x58 with main+0xa49b28's arithmetic, and the native linkers. Quests are split into areas with a loading screen between them (the tester's account of 2026-10-24). Not approved for distribution; r12 and r13 were packaged and never run.
runtime_test: NOT RUN: r25 stops a mask clipping once its row's links are gone, through the class's DTI Enable setter (main+0xa4ba20). r24 ran on Eden 2026-10-24 (installed bytes 6a16c5429a15e761db5b4168586343dfa4ca59e19fdb74143fc00cfd1b74994b): the gauge drew from the quest start - the first run where the mask did not hide it - and vanished at an area transition, with links-lost at t=149.89 and the mask keeping its last rectangle. r23/r22/r20/r18/r14 hid the gauge from the insertion.

limitations: r4 has no runtime test; its lines, the 320-sample budget and the absence of any drawing change are static results.
r2 was built and never run; r3 was run once on Eden and is recorded.
r14 was run once on Eden and failed as reported: the gauge was clipped away from the insertion and the game crashed at the quest end. Its log is the evidence, and the insertion is removed in r15.

r15 was run once on Eden and drew the gauge normally for 740 seconds with no exception; its facts line printed tree_nodes 3 against 4 objects, and its object-list fields were read from the wrong object (the controller's owner field), which is what r16 fixes.

r16 changes nothing on screen: it reads game memory and logs. No drawing, no gauge change, and no cleanup claim (the root-destructor hook fired zero times in the three sessions that logged it). Its Eden run ended in Eden's own shutdown records (maxwell_3d Critical asserts, ForceStop, host SIGSEGV) with zero guest exceptions.
the game's destructor is assumed to free the map block r17 publishes through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator; that free has not been observed, and r17 frees the old 4-word block itself
The per-weapon tier tables live in RomFS weapon data and are not read in this workspace: no weapon data file is extracted here.
The gauge itself is not part of r4.

r25 has not been run. r24's run drew the gauge from the quest start and lost it at an area change, where a mask kept clipping after its links broke; the disable-on-loss path has no runtime evidence, and a mask inserted into a second area's row has never been observed (r24's log ends 12 s after the transition, gauge HUD absent)
